turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: How would you describe robotic surgery adoption in Germany today?
turns.rawText: Interviewer: How would you describe robotic surgery adoption in Germany today?

turns.speaker: Anna Keller
turns.text: It is growing, but adoption is quite uneven. Large university hospitals are much more advanced, while many smaller hospitals are still waiting.
turns.rawText: Anna Keller: It is growing, but adoption is quite uneven. Large university hospitals are much more advanced, while many smaller hospitals are still waiting.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.rawText: Interviewer: What are the main barriers?

turns.speaker: Anna Keller
turns.text: Cost is the first barrier. These are large capital purchases, and hospital finances are under pressure. The second issue is proving that the system will be used enough.
turns.rawText: Anna Keller: Cost is the first barrier. These are large capital purchases, and hospital finances are under pressure. The second issue is proving that the system will be used enough.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.rawText: Interviewer: What does procurement focus on?

turns.speaker: Anna Keller
turns.text: We look at total cost of ownership, expected procedure volume, maintenance, service contracts and training requirements. A strong clinical case helps, but the economic case decides whether it gets approved.
turns.rawText: Anna Keller: We look at total cost of ownership, expected procedure volume, maintenance, service contracts and training requirements. A strong clinical case helps, but the economic case decides whether it gets approved.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.rawText: Interviewer: How important is surgeon training?

turns.speaker: Anna Keller
turns.text: Very important operationally. If the hospital buys a system but only one surgeon is comfortable using it, utilisation will be poor. That weakens the business case.
turns.rawText: Anna Keller: Very important operationally. If the hospital buys a system but only one surgeon is comfortable using it, utilisation will be poor. That weakens the business case.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Do you expect adoption to accelerate?
turns.rawText: Interviewer: Do you expect adoption to accelerate?

turns.speaker: Anna Keller
turns.text: Yes, but I would not expect a dramatic jump. I think growth will be gradual, especially because many hospitals have other competing capital priorities.
turns.rawText: Anna Keller: Yes, but I would not expect a dramatic jump. I think growth will be gradual, especially because many hospitals have other competing capital priorities.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Any rough expectation over the next three to five years?
turns.rawText: Interviewer: Any rough expectation over the next three to five years?

turns.speaker: Anna Keller
turns.text: I would expect continued growth, but probably closer to high single digits or low double digits in procedure volumes rather than something like 20 percent across the whole market.
turns.rawText: Anna Keller: I would expect continued growth, but probably closer to high single digits or low double digits in procedure volumes rather than something like 20 percent across the whole market.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: How long can the purchase process take?
turns.rawText: Interviewer: How long can the purchase process take?

turns.speaker: Anna Keller
turns.text: Nine to eighteen months is common. Procurement, clinical leadership, finance and management all need to align, so it can move slowly.
turns.rawText: Anna Keller: Nine to eighteen months is common. Procurement, clinical leadership, finance and management all need to align, so it can move slowly.
